primary_reviews.rationale: Every quote byte-exact and every count re-derived independently. וָאֵ֣דְעָ֔ה is a wayyiqtol 1cs carrying the cohortative-shaped ending this memoir prefers, the same shape as וָאוֹצְרָ֣ה in v13 and וָאָשִׁ֣יבָה just before, so 'perception-verb hinge' is a morphological description and not a paraphrase. The ve'al yadam disambiguation is the row's strongest work and it holds on syntax rather than on context alone: the sweep gives six book-wide occurrences (MT 3.4, 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.10, 13.13), and in every register instance the phrase is immediately followed by a repair predicate -- וְעַל יָדָ֣ם הֶחֱזִ֗יק, וְעַל יָדָ֖ם הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ -- whereas 13:13 reads וְעַל יָדָ֔ם חָנָ֥ן בֶּן זַכּ֖וּר with no verb at all, a nominal clause assigning rank. That is exactly why it is not a chain-register member, and the row's caution is warranted rather than fussy. The refrain arithmetic is right too: זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י stands at 5:19, 13:14, 13:22 and 13:31 (sweep: 4) inside a six-member family (sweep: 6), making 13:14 the second, as claimed. The 'high' confidence is honest, since both edges rest on tier-1 signals and the next unit opens on its own בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה. One disclosure note that I deliberately do not treat as a defect: the mark data carries a PE keyed to Neh.13.13, one verse inside this close, and the row cites no mark. A Masoretic division between the appointment notice and the prayer is not probative under Writings policy -- not a driver, and not counterevidence -- so the silence costs the row nothing.
The va'edah perception hinge cleanly opens a new grievance once the chamber-cleansing closes, and the zokrah-li close matches the refrain family exactly, echoing 5:19 as claimed.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the cluster's cleanest row and every original-language claim in it survives probing. The 13:23 quote is byte-exact and carries precisely the two ketiv/qere pairs the campaign inventory records for the verse, in the adjacency the row describes: unpointed ketiv אשדודיות followed by pointed qere אַשְׁדֳּדִיּ֔וֹת, then unpointed עמוניות followed by pointed עַמֳּנִיּ֖וֹת. Both are plene-against-defective spellings of the same ethnonyms, and מוֹאֲבִיּֽוֹת carries no variant, so 'both of this verse's ketiv/qere pairs' is exact -- neither undercounted nor padded to three. The opener גַּ֣ם בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם is verified as the second of two (MT 6.17, 13.23; sweep: 2) and the closer זָכְרָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהָ֑י as the sole instance of its sub-form (sweep: 1). The hostile-against-favourable contrast is a real grammatical distinction and not a mood label: 13:29 aims the imperative at a dative of disadvantage, לָהֶ֖ם, and 6:14 at לְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וּלְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט, while 5:19, 13:14, 13:22 and 13:31 all take זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י -- two hostile against four favourable inside the six-member refrain (sweep: 6), so 'the book's only other hostile zokrah besides 6:14' is right. The MT-keyed mark set carries 0 entries across MT 13.23-13.29, so nothing is owed on disclosure, and the row correctly makes no mark claim. The rejected alternative is the genuinely strongest rival at this edge, since 13:30-31 is the neighbouring material best placed to absorb the episode.
Both ketiv/qere pairs in v23 are disclosed exactly where the toolkit's inventory places them, and the zokrah-lahem/zokrah-li distinction is drawn correctly against 6:14's separate hostile sub-form.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening-register claim is well grounded morphologically and I can strengthen it: וְטִֽהַרְתִּ֖ים is waw plus piel qatal 1cs with a 3mp suffix, a summarizing perfect rather than a continuation of the preceding wayyiqtol run, and the narrative form resumes afterwards with וָאַעֲמִ֧ידָה -- the same hiphil cohortative-shaped wayyiqtol with which the memoir stationed the two choirs at 12:31 (וָאַעֲמִ֡ידָה), an unclaimed verbal bracket spanning this whole cluster and better evidence for a closing summary than the row currently offers. The book-close quote is byte-exact and the refrain total is right (sweep: 6 book-wide). The exclusivity attached to that total is not, and it is the kind of claim a digit-bearing sweep next to it can disguise.

challenges.claim: Sweep: 3 book-wide for le-tovah (2:18, 5:19, 13:31), so the row's claim that 13:31 is the only zokrah qualified for good (le-tovah) is false. Neh 5:19 reads זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה against 13:31's זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָֽה: identical in consonants and in vowels, with the difference confined to the cantillation accent on the final word, atnach at 5:19 against silluq at 13:31, which is positional and carries no lexical or semantic weight. Of the three le-tovah hits, 2:18's לַטּוֹבָֽה takes a different preposition in a non-refrain context, leaving exactly 2 zokrah instances so qualified. The adjacent 'sweep: 6 book-wide' backs the refrain count and not the exclusivity, which is why the universals check would have passed this.
challenges.suggested_action: Retract 'the only one qualified for good' and put the stronger true claim in its place: 5:19 and 13:31 are the book's only two zokrah-li-elohai-le-tovah instances (sweep: 2), so the first and the last members of the six-member refrain close on an identical petition. That inclusio supports this row's 'final word' reading far better than the false exclusivity did.

challenges.claim: "the only one qualified 'for good' (le-tovah)" is incorrect. Neh.5:19 closes with the identical four-word clause (זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה) that 13:31 uses (זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָֽה) - consonants and vowel points match exactly; the only difference is a position-appropriate cantillation mark (etnachta at 5:19, mid-clause, versus meteg at 13:31, verse-final), confirmed by direct character inspection and by sweep.py --skel on the full clause (2 book-wide: 5:19, 13:31, not 1). This is an unmarked universal claim that the toolkit's own discipline requires a digit-bearing sweep for, and the digit is 2. The real device is stronger than what's claimed: 13:31 doesn't coin a unique qualifier, it verbatim-reprises the book's first reform-unit close (5:14-19's aside), bracketing the whole back half of the memoir - which supports "giving the memoir its final word" better than a false uniqueness claim does.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the uniqueness claim with the inclusio reading: 13:31 reprises 5:19's exact zokhrah-li-le-tovah clause verbatim, closing the book by echoing its first reform unit rather than coining a new form.

primary_reviews.rationale: The sweep 2 repair fixed v0's false 'only one qualified for good' but installed a universal whose object the sweep does not carry. 'This exact clause, zokhrah-li-elohai-le-tovah, closes only one earlier verse -- 5:19's' is backed by 'sweep: 2 book-wide for the full refrain clause'; I re-ran the sweep and it does return exactly 5:19 and 13:31, but it counts clause OCCURRENCES, whereas the claim is about verse-final POSITION. At 5:19 the clause is verse-initial and the verse runs on past it: זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה. Only 13:31 closes on it. So 'closes only one earlier verse' and 'the first and the last ... close on an identical petition' both overstate what the count establishes - 5:19 closes its unit, but not its verse. Two neighbouring claims do verify: zokrah is 6 book-wide, and the 2:18 exclusion is correctly drawn, since that verse's לַטּוֹבָֽה is article-bearing and idiomatic rather than the refrain's form.
